name: Law firm intake
summary: Take on new clients without missing a conflict check or a time limit. Inquiry, conflict check, consultation, fee proposal and signed engagement, and a written non-engagement letter for everyone else.
description: A time limit may already be running when a prospect first calls, and a missed conflict is hard to undo. This template takes clients on in a fixed order: every inquiry records its practice area, the earliest known time limit, the conflict check and who made it, then the consultation, the fee proposal and the signed engagement. A list of parties supports the conflict search, matters carry the power of attorney date and a retention date, and declined or silent prospects get a written non-engagement letter. It holds a pointer to the case, never case facts, privileged content, health data or opponents' details. It is not matter management, trust accounting, a procedural deadline authority or billing.

page.headline: Law firm intake that never misses a conflict check or a time limit, built by your AI agent
page.answer: A law firm intake takes a prospect from the first inquiry to a signed engagement in a fixed order: the earliest known time limit, the conflict check, the consultation, the fee proposal and the agreement, with a written non-engagement letter for everyone who is not taken on. Paste this template into your AI agent and it builds the intake desk in Customermates. You approve the plan before anything is built, and case facts stay out.

routine.title: The intake desk routine
steps: Record every new inquiry the same day: practice area, how the person found you, the parties involved and the earliest known time limit.
Triage inquiries with a time limit inside 14 days first: accept, refer out or warn the person the same day.
Run the conflict check before any advice: search the parties, clients and former clients, and record the result and who made it.
Send the fee proposal the day after the consultation, and follow up after three days if you hear nothing.
Once the agreement is signed, collect the advance and chase it after a week. Open the matter in your case system.
Send the written non-engagement letter to everyone you decline or who goes silent, so there is a record that no relationship was formed.

limits: It is not your case system. Documents, time records, procedural deadlines and court filings stay in your case software; a matter here is a pointer.
It is not a deadline authority. The only date held at intake is the earliest known time limit, to decide what to look at first. Procedural deadlines stay in the system you rely on.
It does no trust accounting or billing. There is no invoice model: the advance is recorded as a date, and the ledger stays in your accounting system.
The conflict check is a human aid. You search the list of parties yourself and record the result; Customermates cannot stop you from opening a matter.
It is not a client portal or an e-signature tool. A signed agreement is a link to the signed file.
Keep case facts, privileged content, health data and details of opponents out. Customermates has no field-level permissions, so what is in a list is visible to everyone who has access to that list.

faq.question: What does a law firm intake process include?
faq.answer: Practitioner checklists run: inquiry, screening with conflict check and urgency, consultation, fee and engagement terms, signed agreement with power of attorney and advance, and only then the matter in the case system. Firms differ on details such as whether the advance comes before work starts. The template fixes the order and lets you set the rest.

faq.question: Should the conflict check come before the consultation?
faq.answer: Guidance from the American Bar Association's young lawyers and German practice sources put the conflict check before any advice and before the engagement letter; one checklist even runs it before the first consultation. The template has a screening step before the consultation and records the result and who made it. Rules differ by country, so check your own professional rules.

faq.question: Why record a time limit at first contact?
faq.answer: A limitation period can run out before you accept the case, and commentary in German practice magazines notes that an avoidable lapse can create liability even before acceptance. Recording the earliest known time limit and where it comes from lets you triage what is urgent the same day. It is a triage date, not a deadline calendar.

faq.question: Do I need a non-engagement letter?
faq.answer: It is good practice: guidance for lawyers recommends a written letter to prospects you decline or who do not retain you, so there is a record that no relationship was formed. The template creates an Action to write it when you decline an inquiry or a prospect does not retain you. Whether it is required depends on your country.

faq.question: Can I put client matters in Customermates?
faq.answer: Only as pointers: a reference to the matter in your case system. Keep case facts, privileged content, health data and details of opponents out, because Customermates has no field-level permissions. The agent sends nothing and creates no sample records; drafts exist only when you ask for them.
